free_tier.stated: SparkCloud publishes a six-part free stack on one account: Containers (ubuntu 24.04, root, real ssh), Spaces (VS Code in a tab, auto-hibernates), Databases (postgres 16, daily backups), Tiles (static hosting, custom domains), AI & agents (openai-compatible, claude, gpt, gemini) and CDN storage (object storage, global edge). The page states 'Free for every teen, no credit card, because a nonprofit covers the cost' and '$0 forever, no credit card', and names The Spark Forward Foundation, a 501(c)(3) nonprofit, as the operator. No credit figure, container shape, or monthly hour allowance is published on the page read.

chaining: Supplies database, object store, static hosting, AI endpoints, and virtual machine capacity under a single identity with no credit card required. Eligibility requires youth age verification.

limits.value: The age verification is the binding constraint and it is a gate rather than a quota: 'Every account is age-verified', so an adult outside the stated range cannot reach any of the six components, and no amount of usage planning changes that.

notes: Recorded because the corpus stops the next session from chasing it, and because the shape is instructive: a nonprofit can publish a stack that no commercial provider matches on breadth, and gate it on an attribute rather than on money. The quota is unknown, which matters if the age policy ever widens; the page publishes no credit number, no container shape and no monthly hour allowance, so a reader who found the door open would still not know what was behind it. FreeTierWatch and a Hacker News thread both discuss Oracle's halving in the same week, which is how this lead was found.

wave2.provider_as_written: SparkCloud (The Spark Forward Foundation): a full free cloud stack that is age-gated to teenagers (refutation, record the door)
